source.text: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ μέγα καὶ θαυμαστόν, ἀγγέλους ἑπτὰ ἔχοντας πληγὰς ἑπτὰ τὰς ἐσχάτας, ὅτι ἐν αὐταῖς ἐτελέσθη ὁ θυμὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw another sign in the heaven great and wonderful, angels seven having plagues seven the last, because in them was completed the wrath of the God.

en.L: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and wonderful: seven angels having seven plagues, the last ones, because in them the wrath of God is completed.
en.B: Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and astonishing: seven angels with seven plagues, the last plagues, for with them God's wrath is brought to an end.
en.R: Then I saw another great and amazing sign in heaven. There were seven angels with seven plagues. These are the last plagues, because they finish God's anger.

fr.L: Et je vis dans le ciel un autre signe, grand et merveilleux : sept anges ayant sept fléaux, les derniers, car en eux s’achève la fureur de Dieu.
fr.B: Puis je vis dans le ciel un autre signe, grand et étonnant : sept anges qui tenaient sept fléaux, les derniers, car avec eux la colère de Dieu arrive à son terme.
fr.R: Puis j’ai vu dans le ciel un autre signe, grand et extraordinaire. Il y avait sept anges avec sept fléaux. Ce sont les derniers fléaux, parce qu’avec eux la colère de Dieu prend fin.

es.L: Y vi otra señal en el cielo, grande y admirable: siete ángeles que tenían siete plagas, las últimas, porque en ellas se ha consumado la ira de Dios.
es.B: Vi en el cielo otra señal, grande y asombrosa: siete ángeles con siete plagas, las últimas, porque con ellas la ira de Dios llega a su fin.
es.R: Luego vi en el cielo otra señal grande y asombrosa. Había siete ángeles con siete plagas. Son las últimas plagas, porque con ellas termina la ira de Dios.

decisions.choice: the last plagues: God's wrath brought to completion
decisions.reason: After the seals and trumpets, the bowls (chapter 16) are the last series of judgments. ἐτελέσθη is a past tense used of what is sure: with them God's wrath reaches its end. The three signs of the book are the woman (12:1), the dragon (12:3), and now these angels.

decisions.choice: sign
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term, kept at every level.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R): "je vis" / "j’ai vu"; historic presents kept at Literal ("ils chantent")
decisions.reason: John tells what he saw; the passé simple is the tense of careful written narrative, the passé composé the tense Readable uses throughout. Where the Greek has a present for an ongoing scene (15:3), Balanced and Readable use the imperfect. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: fléaux
decisions.reason: "Plaies" is the traditional word for the plagues of Egypt but today means wounds first; "fléaux" says disasters sent as judgment and is the plain word at every level.

decisions.choice: se ha consumado (L); llega a su fin (B); termina (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring to its end, so these plagues finish God's wrath, as the meaning decision says. "Consumar" says that at Literal; Balanced and Readable use plainer words.

source.text: Καὶ εἶδον ὡς θάλασσαν ὑαλίνην μεμιγμένην πυρί, καὶ τοὺς νικῶντας ἐκ τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τῆς εἰκόνος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν τὴν ὑαλίνην, ἔχοντας κιθάρας τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw as a sea glassy having been mixed with fire, and those overcoming out of the beast and out of the image of it and out of the number of the name of it standing on the sea the glassy, having harps of the God.

en.L: And I saw [something] like a sea of glass mixed with fire, and those who had overcome the beast and its image and the number of its name, standing by the sea of glass, holding harps of God.
en.B: I saw something like a sea of glass with fire mingled in it. By the glassy sea stood those who had overcome the beast, its image, and the number of its name, and they held harps of God.
en.R: I saw something that looked like a sea of glass mixed with fire. Standing beside it were the people who had won the victory over the beast, its statue, and the number of its name. God had given them harps to hold.

fr.L: Et je vis comme une mer de verre mêlée de feu, et ceux qui sont sortis vainqueurs de la bête et de son image et du nombre de son nom, se tenant près de la mer de verre, ayant des harpes de Dieu.
fr.B: Je vis comme une mer de verre où se mêlait du feu. Au bord de cette mer de verre se tenaient ceux qui avaient vaincu la bête, son image et le nombre de son nom ; ils tenaient des harpes de Dieu.
fr.R: J’ai vu quelque chose qui ressemblait à une mer de verre mêlée de feu. Au bord de cette mer, il y avait les gens qui avaient remporté la victoire sur la bête, sur sa statue et sur le nombre de son nom. Dieu leur avait donné des harpes.

es.L: Y vi [algo] como un mar de vidrio mezclado con fuego, y a los que habían vencido a la bestia y a su imagen y al número de su nombre, de pie junto al mar de vidrio, con arpas de Dios.
es.B: Vi algo como un mar de vidrio mezclado con fuego. Junto al mar de vidrio estaban de pie los que habían vencido a la bestia, a su imagen y al número de su nombre, y tenían arpas que Dios les había dado.
es.R: Vi algo que parecía un mar de vidrio mezclado con fuego. Junto a él estaban de pie las personas que habían ganado la victoria sobre la bestia, sobre su estatua y sobre el número de su nombre. Dios les había dado arpas para que las tocaran.

decisions.choice: a sea of glass mixed with fire, and the victors beside it: the crossing of the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The sea of glass is the one before the throne (4:6), now mixed with fire, the fire of judgment. The victors stand beside it and sing the song of Moses (15:3), as Israel stood on the shore of the Red Sea and sang after God brought them through and judged their enemies (Exodus 14-15).

decisions.choice: those who overcame: they came out victorious over the beast
decisions.reason: νικῶντας with ἐκ, "out of", is unusual: they have overcome and come out free from the beast, its image and its number (13:14-18). Their victory was faithfulness, even to death (12:11).

decisions.choice: on or beside the sea
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ with this case can mean "on" or "by". Like Israel at the Red Sea, they most likely stand on its shore.

decisions.choice: harps of God: given by God, for his praise
decisions.reason: The genitive can mean harps that belong to God's worship or harps God has given (compare 5:8; 14:2).

decisions.choice: sortis vainqueurs de (L)
decisions.reason: French "sortir vainqueur de" keeps the Greek "out of" after the verb and says what it means (m2): they came out of the struggle victorious.

decisions.choice: junto al mar
decisions.reason: The Greek preposition can mean on or beside, as the meaning decision says; with the picture of the Red Sea crossing, Spanish follows the English in placing them beside the sea.

decisions.choice: arpas que Dios les había dado
decisions.reason: "Harps of God" means harps given by God for his praise, as the meaning decision says; Balanced says so, since Spanish "arpas de Dios" would suggest the harps belong to God. Literal keeps the Greek phrase.

source.text: καὶ ᾄδουσιν τὴν ᾠδὴν Μωϋσέως τοῦ δούλου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν ᾠδὴν τοῦ ἀρνίου λέγοντες· Μεγάλα καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ· δίκαιαι καὶ ἀληθιναὶ αἱ ὁδοί σου, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν αἰώνων·

records.literal_gloss: And they sing the song of Moses the slave of the God and the song of the Lamb, saying: Great and wonderful the works of you, Lord the God the Almighty; righteous and true the ways of you, the King of the ages.

en.L: And they sing the song of Moses the slave of God and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and wonderful [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works, Lord God the Almighty; righteous and true [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways, King of the ages.
en.B: They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb: "How great and wonderful are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works, Lord God, the Almighty! Your ways are just and true, King of the ages!
en.R: They sing the song of Moses, God's servant, and the song of the Lamb: "Lord God, the Almighty, the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do are great and wonderful! King forever, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways are right and true!

fr.L: Et ils chantent le chant de Moïse, l’esclave de Dieu, et le chant de l’Agneau, disant : « Grandes et merveilleuses [sont] {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} œuvres, Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant ; justes et vraies [sont] {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} voies, Roi des siècles.
fr.B: Ils chantaient le chant de Moïse, le serviteur de Dieu, et le chant de l’Agneau : « Que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} œuvres sont grandes et merveilleuses, Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant ! Tes voies sont justes et vraies, Roi des siècles !
fr.R: Ils chantaient le chant de Moïse, le serviteur de Dieu, et le chant de l’Agneau : « Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant, ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais est grand et merveilleux ! Roi pour toujours, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} façon d’agir est juste et vraie !

es.L: Y cantan el cántico de Moisés, el esclavo de Dios, y el cántico del Cordero, diciendo: «Grandes y admirables [son] {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} obras, Señor Dios Todopoderoso; justos y verdaderos [son] {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caminos, Rey de los siglos.
es.B: Cantaban el cántico de Moisés, el siervo de Dios, y el cántico del Cordero: «¡Qué grandes y maravillosas son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} obras, Señor Dios Todopoderoso! ¡Justos y verdaderos son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caminos, Rey de los siglos!
es.R: Cantaban el cántico de Moisés, el siervo de Dios, y el cántico del Cordero: «Señor Dios Todopoderoso, ¡las cosas que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} haces son grandes y maravillosas! Rey eterno, ¡{{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caminos son rectos y verdaderos!

decisions.choice: the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb: a new exodus
decisions.reason: Moses and Israel sang after crossing the Red Sea (Exodus 15), and Moses taught Israel a song of God's faithfulness (Deuteronomy 32). The song of the Lamb is the same song: the Lamb's victory is the greater exodus, and it is sung by those he has set free. Moses is called God's slave as in Numbers 12:7 and Joshua 1:2.

decisions.choice: great and wonderful works, just and true ways: the psalms and Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The words are drawn from the Old Testament: "Great are the works of the LORD" (Psalm 111:2), "wonderful are your works" (Psalm 139:14), "all his ways are justice ... just and upright is he" (Deuteronomy 32:4).

decisions.choice: King of the ages
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads αἰώνων, "of the ages". Other manuscripts read "of the nations", which fits Jeremiah 10:7 and the next verse; later ones read "of the saints". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: King of the ages (L, B); King forever (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "of the ages" means.

decisions.choice: your: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The song is sung to God.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: God is addressed as "tu", and "tu", "te", "toi", "ton", "ta", "tes" carry the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the French style guide (§6, §7): God is addressed with "tu", and the second-person forms take the span wherever the English "you", "your" does; a form at the start of a sentence is written plainly ("Tes voies").

decisions.choice: l’esclave (L); le serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the French term sheet (§5) and the English.

decisions.choice: Rey de los siglos (L, B); Rey eterno (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the text the English follows, with "siglos" for "ages" as in the doxology formula of the book; Readable says "Rey eterno", as the English Readable says "King forever". Moses is "esclavo" at Literal and "siervo" at Balanced and Readable, the settled steps.

source.text: τίς οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇ, κύριε, καὶ δοξάσει τὸ ὄνομά σου, ὅτι μόνος ὅσιος;

records.literal_gloss: Who not not will fear, Lord, and will glorify the name of you? because alone holy;

en.L: Who will not fear [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}], Lord, and glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name? For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone [are] holy.
en.B: Lord, who will not fear and glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name? Only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are holy.
en.R: Lord, everyone will fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and give glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, because only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are holy.

fr.L: Qui ne [{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}] craindra pas, Seigneur, et ne glorifiera pas {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ? Car {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} seul [es] saint.
fr.B: Seigneur, qui ne craindrait pas et ne glorifierait pas {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ? Car {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} seul es saint.
fr.R: Seigneur, tout le monde {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} craindra et rendra gloire à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, parce que {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} seul es saint.

es.L: ¿Quién no temerá, Señor, y no glorificará {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre? Porque solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} [eres] santo.
es.B: Señor, ¿quién no temerá y no glorificará {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre? Solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres santo.
es.R: Señor, todos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} temerán y darán gloria a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre, porque solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres santo.

decisions.choice: Who will not fear you? Jeremiah 10:7
decisions.reason: "Who would not fear you, O King of the nations?" (Jeremiah 10:7). The question expects the answer: no one. Everyone will fear and honor God.

decisions.choice: alone holy
decisions.reason: ὅσιος means holy in the sense of pure and faithful. Only God is wholly so; no beast or ruler may claim it.

decisions.choice: a statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into what it means: everyone will fear God (m1).

decisions.choice: ¿Quién no temerá ... {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre?
decisions.reason: The Greek gives "fear" no object of its own; the English Literal supplies "you" in brackets, but Spanish can let "tu nombre" serve as the object of both verbs, so Literal needs no supplied word.

source.text: ὅτι πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιόν σου, ὅτι τὰ δικαιώματά σου ἐφανερώθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: because all the nations will come and will worship before you, because the righteous acts of you were revealed.

en.L: For all the nations will come and worship before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteous acts have been revealed."
en.B: Every nation will come and worship in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} acts of justice are now plain for all to see."
en.R: All the nations will come and worship {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because everyone has seen the right things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done."

fr.L: Car toutes les nations viendront et adoreront devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, car {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} actes de justice ont été manifestés. »
fr.B: Toutes les nations viendront adorer en {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} présence, car {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} actes de justice sont maintenant visibles aux yeux de tous. »
fr.R: Toutes les nations viendront {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}adorer, parce que tout le monde a vu ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait de juste. »

es.L: Porque todas las naciones vendrán y adorarán delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} actos de justicia han sido manifestados».
es.B: Todas las naciones vendrán y adorarán en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} presencia, porque {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} actos de justicia ya están a la vista de todos».
es.R: Todas las naciones vendrán y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} adorarán, porque todos han visto las cosas justas que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has hecho».

decisions.choice: all the nations will come and worship: Psalm 86:9
decisions.reason: "All the nations you have made shall come and worship before you, O Lord, and shall glorify your name" (Psalm 86:9). The hope of the nations' worship runs through the book (5:9; 7:9; 21:24-26).

decisions.choice: your righteous acts: God's just deeds, including his judgments
decisions.reason: δικαιώματά can mean righteous deeds or just decrees. Here it is God's acts of justice, now made plain for all to see.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} actos de justicia
decisions.reason: The Greek word names righteous acts, God's just deeds including his judgments, as the meaning decision says; "actos de justicia" keeps the wider sense, where "juicios" would narrow it.

source.text: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ πληγὰς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ, ἐνδεδυμένοι λίνον καθαρὸν λαμπρὸν καὶ περιεζωσμένοι περὶ τὰ στήθη ζώνας χρυσᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: And after these things I saw, and was opened the temple of the tent of the testimony in the heaven, \v 6 and came out the seven angels the [ones] having the seven plagues out of the temple, having been clothed in linen pure bright and having been girded around the chests with sashes golden.

en.L: And after these things I looked, and the temple of the tent of witness in heaven was opened, \v 6 and the seven angels who had the seven plagues came out of the temple, clothed in pure, bright linen and with golden sashes wrapped around their chests.
en.B: Then I looked, and in heaven the temple, the tent of witness, stood open. \v 6 From the temple the seven angels who held the seven plagues came out, robed in pure linen that shone, with gold sashes bound around their chests.
en.R: After this I looked, and I saw that the temple in heaven was open. It was the tent where God's covenant was kept. \v 6 The seven angels with the seven plagues came out of the temple. They wore clean, shining linen clothes and gold sashes around their chests.

fr.L: Et après cela je vis, et le temple de la tente du témoignage dans le ciel fut ouvert, \v 6 et les sept anges qui avaient les sept fléaux sortirent du temple, vêtus d’un lin pur, éclatant, et portant autour de la poitrine des ceintures d’or.
fr.B: Après cela, je regardai, et dans le ciel le temple, la tente du témoignage, était ouvert. \v 6 Du temple sortirent les sept anges qui tenaient les sept fléaux, vêtus d’un lin pur et resplendissant, avec des ceintures d’or nouées autour de la poitrine.
fr.R: Après cela, j’ai regardé, et j’ai vu que le temple du ciel était ouvert. C’était la tente où l’on gardait l’alliance de Dieu. \v 6 Les sept anges qui avaient les sept fléaux sont sortis du temple. Ils portaient des vêtements de lin propres et brillants, et des ceintures d’or autour de la poitrine.

es.L: Y después de estas cosas miré, y se abrió el templo del tabernáculo del testimonio en el cielo, \v 6 y salieron del templo los siete ángeles que tenían las siete plagas, vestidos de lino puro y resplandeciente, y ceñidos alrededor del pecho con cintos de oro.
es.B: Después miré, y en el cielo estaba abierto el templo, el tabernáculo del testimonio. \v 6 Del templo salieron los siete ángeles que tenían las siete plagas, vestidos de lino puro y resplandeciente, con cintos de oro ceñidos alrededor del pecho.
es.R: Después de esto miré, y vi que el templo del cielo estaba abierto. Era la tienda donde se guardaba el pacto de Dios. \v 6 Los siete ángeles que tenían las siete plagas salieron del templo. Llevaban ropa de lino limpia y brillante, y cintos de oro alrededor del pecho.

decisions.choice: the tent of witness: the tabernacle that held the covenant
decisions.reason: In the wilderness the tabernacle was called "the tent of witness" because it held the tablets of the covenant, the testimony (Exodus 38:21; Numbers 9:15; 17:7; Acts 7:44). The judgments come from the place of God's covenant: they are his faithfulness to it.

decisions.choice: linen
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads λίνον, "linen". Some important manuscripts read a word that differs by one letter and means "stone" (compare Ezekiel 28:13). The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: linen and gold sashes: the dress of priests
decisions.reason: Priests wore linen (Leviticus 16:4), and the risen Christ wears a golden sash (1:13). The angels come out of the temple as priests serving God.

decisions.choice: the tent where God's covenant was kept (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the tent of witness" (m1).

decisions.choice: la tente du témoignage (L, B); la tente où l’on gardait l’alliance de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: "Tente" says plainly what the tabernacle was; "tabernacle" in French now mostly means the box for the sacrament. Readable explains the phrase with "l’alliance", the term sheet's word for covenant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: el tabernáculo del testimonio (L, B); la tienda donde se guardaba el pacto de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: "Tabernáculo" is the Spanish name for the tent of meeting in the wilderness, and "testimonio" is the covenant law kept in it, as the meaning decision says; Readable says what it was, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἓν ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων ἔδωκεν τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις ἑπτὰ φιάλας χρυσᾶς γεμούσας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.

records.literal_gloss: And one of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven bowls golden being full of the fury of the God the [one] living into the ages of the ages.

en.L: And one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the fury of God, who lives for the ages of the ages.
en.B: One of the four living creatures handed the seven angels seven gold bowls, full to the brim with the fury of the God who lives forever and ever.
en.R: One of the four living creatures gave each of the seven angels a gold bowl. The bowls were full of the anger of God, who lives forever and ever.

fr.L: Et l’un des quatre êtres vivants donna aux sept anges sept coupes d’or pleines de la fureur de Dieu, qui vit pour les siècles des siècles.
fr.B: L’un des quatre êtres vivants remit aux sept anges sept coupes d’or, remplies jusqu’au bord de la fureur du Dieu qui vit pour toujours et à jamais.
fr.R: L’un des quatre êtres vivants a donné à chacun des sept anges une coupe d’or. Les coupes étaient pleines de la colère de Dieu, qui vit pour toujours et à jamais.

es.L: Y uno de los cuatro seres vivientes dio a los siete ángeles siete copas de oro llenas del furor de Dios, que vive por los siglos de los siglos.
es.B: Uno de los cuatro seres vivientes entregó a los siete ángeles siete copas de oro, llenas hasta el borde del furor del Dios que vive por los siglos de los siglos.
es.R: Uno de los cuatro seres vivientes les dio a cada uno de los siete ángeles una copa de oro. Las copas estaban llenas de la ira de Dios, que vive para siempre.

decisions.choice: golden bowls: the bowls of worship, now filled with wrath
decisions.reason: φιάλας are wide, shallow bowls used in temple worship. In 5:8 golden bowls held the prayers of the saints; now golden bowls hold God's wrath. The prayers are being answered.

decisions.choice: coupes
decisions.reason: The vessels are the wide, shallow bowls of temple worship (m1); "coupes" is the French word that fits them and the cup of wrath of 14:10, where "bols" sounds domestic and "fioles" means small bottles.

decisions.choice: copas
decisions.reason: These are the same bowls of worship as in 5:8, now filled with wrath, as the meaning decision says, so Spanish keeps "copas", the word chosen there, for the seven bowls through the book.

source.text: καὶ ἐγεμίσθη ὁ ναὸς καπνοῦ ἐκ τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἄχρι τελεσθῶσιν αἱ ἑπτὰ πληγαὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων.

records.literal_gloss: And was filled the temple with smoke from the glory of the God and from the power of him, and no one was able to enter into the temple until were completed the seven plagues of the seven angels.

en.L: And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.
en.B: Smoke from God's glory and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power filled the temple, and no one was able to enter it until the seven angels' seven plagues were finished.
en.R: The temple was filled with smoke, because God's glory and power were there. No one could go into the temple until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven plagues.

fr.L: Et le temple fut rempli de fumée [venant] de la gloire de Dieu et de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance, et personne ne pouvait entrer dans le temple jusqu’à ce que soient achevés les sept fléaux des sept anges.
fr.B: La fumée de la gloire de Dieu et de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance remplit le temple, et personne ne put y entrer avant que les sept fléaux des sept anges soient terminés.
fr.R: Le temple s’est rempli de fumée, parce que la gloire et la puissance de Dieu étaient là. Personne ne pouvait entrer dans le temple avant que les sept anges aient fini de verser les sept fléaux.

es.L: Y el templo se llenó de humo por la gloria de Dios y por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder, y nadie podía entrar en el templo hasta que se cumplieran las siete plagas de los siete ángeles.
es.B: El humo de la gloria de Dios y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder llenó el templo, y nadie pudo entrar en él hasta que terminaron las siete plagas de los siete ángeles.
es.R: El templo se llenó de humo, porque la gloria y el poder de Dios estaban allí. Nadie podía entrar en el templo hasta que los siete ángeles terminaran de derramar las siete plagas.

decisions.choice: smoke filling the temple: God's glory at the tabernacle and temple
decisions.reason: When the tabernacle was finished, the glory of the LORD filled it and Moses could not enter (Exodus 40:34-35); at Solomon's temple the priests could not stand to minister (1 Kings 8:10-11); Isaiah saw the house filled with smoke (Isaiah 6:4). No one can enter or intercede until the judgments are done.
